description: NovoSriti is a team passionate about exploring the stories behind humanity’s journey into space. We aim to bring forgotten missions and abandoned equipment back into focus, turning them into stories of exploration, innovation, challenges, and discovery. Through technology and storytelling, we hope to preserve these pieces of space history and make them accessible to everyone.
summary: Mission Remnants is a live, story-driven learning website that turns the history of retired space hardware into a journey students can actually follow. Learners move through six mission chapters, explore 3D models of the machines, check every explanation against linked sources, ask an AI mission assistant when they get stuck, and then try simplified challenges in Mission Lab. We built it for curious students who get lost in scattered reports and technical jargon, so they can see why each mission mattered. We are NovoSriti, a student team from Chattogram, Bangladesh.
details: Mission Remnants The missions ended. Their stories remain. Space exploration doesn't end when a spacecraft stops communicating or a mission reaches its final day. The machines we leave behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond still have stories to tell. They represent years of human curiosity, scientific effort, engineering, and discovery. Yet, many of these stories remain difficult for younger generations to discover and understand. That's where Mission Remnants, developed by Team NovoSriti, comes in. Our project is an interactive, educational experience designed to help young learners, especially children aged 8–12, discover the stories behind humanity's space missions and the spacecraft and equipment left behind. Instead of simply presenting dates, technical information, or scientific reports, we bring these missions to life through engaging storytelling, interactive chapters, and a mission-based learning experience. Through our Chapters, users can explore the history of different missions, understand why specific spacecraft were sent, learn about their instruments and objectives, and discover what they contributed to science. Our Mission Lab takes learning a step further by allowing users to engage with mission-related activities and better understand the challenges and objectives these machines were designed to accomplish. We believe that children learn better when they can connect with what they are learning. That's why we chose to combine scientific information with storytelling and interactive exploration rather than making another website filled with complicated facts. The project aims to make space science more accessible, particularly for young learners who may find traditional scientific resources difficult to follow. By connecting engineering, history, and science through an engaging experience, we hope to encourage curiosity, critical thinking, and a deeper appreciation of human exploration. What makes Mission Remnants different is its perspective. We aren't only interested in the moment a spacecraft launches or the discoveries it makes. We also want to explore what happens afterward. What remains when the mission is over? What did these machines teach us? And why should their stories still matter? We built the project around NASA's mission information and educational resources, prioritizing scientific accuracy and reliable sources. Our development process also involved web technologies, interactive 3D resources, and AI-assisted tools to support the design and development process. We aimed to make the experience visually engaging without allowing presentation to overshadow the science. Throughout development, our team considered the accuracy of information, the intended age group, ease of navigation, educational value, and the limitations of the available resources. We wanted to create something that was not only interesting to explore but also meaningful to learn from. Ultimately, Mission Remnants is our way of reminding people that even when a mission ends, its contribution to humanity does not. Every abandoned lander, rover, and spacecraft represents a chapter in our journey to understand the universe. The missions ended. Their stories remain. And we believe those stories deserve to be remembered.
